newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed a touch firmer, returning to the levels before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan unnerved world markets last Friday.
Dealers said that in thin cash trading, guilder state loans tracked German Bund futures, which bounced around in volatile trading.
"This morning there was some optimism in the market. We dipped in the afternoon but it was just a little too deep. That's the reason we bounced back," said a trader.
At 5.72 percent, the closing 10-year yield is almost 90 basis points below the peak this year.
One dealer noted interest to buy July 1998 bonds and to sell 2005 and 2006 maturities.
Dealers said a mix of U.S. data today had no impact, as the market was instead looking ahead to November U.S. data this week for indications of where U.S. interest rates were heading.
Producer prices are out on Wednesday and inflation and retail sales on Thursday.
